summary:
No slate data was provided today, so this briefing leans on what the model carries forward: a quiet 14-day window across the board (all four ratings show 0-0, n=0 on every category) means there's no fresh hot/cold signal to chase — this is late-season sample drought, not a system malfunction. The one live thread worth tracking is the SP category streak, which sits at 3W across R1 through R4, and the bullpen_fatigue category, which is mired in a 5L skid across all four ratings. If today's games lean on starting-pitcher-driven picks, ride that momentum; if the lean is toward bullpen fatigue reads, fade or size down until that streak breaks. The 30-day strong-play window also backs R2 as the sharpest unit right now at 80% (4-1, +3.0u) versus R1 and R3 both sitting at 75% (3-1, +1.0u each) and R4 matching at 75% (3-1, +1.0u) — thin samples, but if R2 and another rating agree on a strong play today, that's your highest-confidence stack.

Category combos remain the backbone of this model's long-term edge, and they haven't moved: trends+sp leads at 58% (370-268, n=638), with trends+runs (57.3%, 404-301) and trends+bullpen (56.8%, 391-297) close behind. Any today's-slate pick where trends and sp both agree should be treated as the default top play, especially given sp's active 3W streak riding shotgun. On team trust, go straight to the top tier if any of these names are on the board and the model likes them: LAD's strong-play record is elite at 80% (28-7, +27.0u) and BOS sits at 76% (22-7, +19.0u) — both clear the bar for a max-confidence look. TBR (70%, +21.0u strong) and MIL (69%, +18.0u strong) round out the trust tier on volume. Conversely, if NYY shows up as a liked side today, size down hard — strong plays on them are underwater at 39% (9-14, -4.0u), the only team leader bleeding units. With trends+sp agreement, an active SP streak, and a top-tier team like LAD or BOS in the frame, that's the identifiable sweet spot to target on today's card; everything else should be sized to the thin 30-day samples until more data populates the 7/14-day windows.
